newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to enter oil, gas ventures in 120 days.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to enter oil, gas ventures in 120 days.

text.p: Brazil's state-owned petroleum giant Petrobras will enter its first joint ventures with private companies in oil and gas production and exploration and in the petrochemical sector within 120 days, Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito said Wednesday.
"The first partnerships involving Petrobras be in the area of exploration and production or in chemical or gas production will take place within 120 days as of now," Brito said.
The minister was speaking to reporters after President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed into law a bill which regulates the opening up of Brazil's petroleum industry to private competition.
The bill was approved by Congress earlier this year.
The minister said a new National Petroleum Agency (ANP), which will act as a regulator for the sector, would be up and running within 120 days.

Petrobras has 90 days to inform the government which areas where it is currently producing or exploring oil and gas it will want to retain and which areas may be opened up for private companies or groups to carry out their own exploration and production.

Brito said as well as several proposed joint ventures between Petrobras and private groups for oil and gas exploration and production Petrobras was also mulling a proposed thermoelectric power plant and a petrochemical unit.
Petrobras would hold a minority stake of about 30 percent in both projects, the minister said.
